# Erdős Problem 259

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/259](https://www.erdosproblems.com/259)
-/

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.Moebius

namespace Erdos259

/--
Is $\sum_{n} \mu(n)^2\frac{n}{2^n}$ irrational?

This is true, and was proved by Chen and Ruzsa.

[ChRu99] Chen, Yong-Gao and Ruzsa, Imre Z., On the irrationality of certain series. Period. Math. Hungar. (1999), 31--37.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/c7429943f6b3a634797dc8b2a3b01f2d/raw/8c6b5b7f08021f0aed2312542dd2e9ee7beaa6d6/Erdos259.lean"]
theorem erdos_259 : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (μ n) ^ 2 * n / (2 ^ n)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos259

reformulations.difference: Erdős's original 1988 formulation uses ∑ₖ qₖ/2^{qₖ}, where qₖ enumerates the positive squarefree integers. Lean instead uses ∑ₙ μ(n)² n/2ⁿ over all natural numbers, exactly as the current problem webpage does.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib's μ(n)² is the indicator of Squarefree n. The n = 0 summand is zero. Squarefree natural numbers form an infinite set containing every prime, so their increasing Nat.nth enumeration lists each exactly once; reindexing therefore gives equality of the two series. Moreover, the summands lie between 0 and n/2ⁿ, proving summability and agreement with the ordinary convergent series. The equality and irrationality equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review259.series_eq_squarefree_enumeration and Review259.original_source_iff, without sorryAx.

review.notes:
The sole declaration faithfully states the affirmative solution. Lean inspection confirms that exponentiation, multiplication, and division in the summand occur in ℝ, not using integer division. Scratch checks verified the terms at 0, 1, 2, and 4, denominator nonvanishing, summability, and equivalence with positive-natural indexing. The source's stronger infinite-subseries result is not claimed by this file.

The research-solved tag and formal-proof record agree with the source's PROVED (LEAN) status. The linked proof's final statement is equivalent to the repository statement by Int.cast_pow, also proved in the scratch file. The linked text contains no literal sorry or custom axioms, but replaying it unmodified under the supplied Lean 4.33.1/Mathlib produced elaboration/API errors; I therefore did not independently certify that external proof. This does not establish a status discrepancy. The full Chen–Ruzsa article was inaccessible, but the exact problem-page source and Erdős's original formulation were available and sufficient to settle statement faithfulness.
